description: A reusable unit of packages, files, scripts, and environment.

children.description: Command the alias expands to, written in the syntax of the shell it is generated for. It may carry arguments, pipes and quotes: cfgd quotes the whole value per dialect when it writes the alias definition, so the text reaches the shell exactly as declared. Required — an alias with no command has nothing to expand to.
children.name: command

children.description: Alias name, as typed at the shell prompt.
children.name: name

children.description: Platform tags gating this entry alone. Empty means every platform the declaring module or profile is not already gated off of. Tags are matched against the machine's OS, distro, and arch; use `macos` for macOS. An entry gated off this host is not part of its desired state at all: it appears on no surface, exactly as a platform-filtered package does.
children.name: platforms

fields.description: Names of other modules this one requires; cfgd resolves and applies them first.
fields.name: depends

children.description: Variable name. Must be shell-safe and not a reserved `CFGD_*` name.
children.name: name

children.description: Platform tags gating this entry alone. Empty means every platform the declaring module or profile is not already gated off of. Tags are matched against the machine's OS, distro, and arch; use `macos` for macOS. An entry gated off this host is not part of its desired state at all: it appears on no surface, exactly as a platform-filtered package does.
children.name: platforms

children.description: Value assigned to the variable, exported verbatim into the shell environment.
children.name: value

children.description: The encryption backend to use (e.g. "sops", "age").
children.name: backend

children.description: When encryption must be enforced. Defaults to `InRepo`.
children.name: mode

children.description: Encryption settings for this module file.
children.name: encryption

children.description: Keys/values to deep-merge into the target, leaving unmentioned keys untouched. Values are literal (no template rendering). Mutually exclusive with `script`.
children.name: ensure

children.description: File format to parse the target as. Inferred from the target's extension when omitted.
children.name: format

children.description: A script path or an inline command that receives the target's current content on stdin and writes the new content to stdout. A relative path resolves against the module directory for a module file (`spec.files[]`) and against the config directory for a profile file (`spec.files.managed[]`); a value that resolves to no file is run as an inline command. Mutually exclusive with `ensure`.
children.name: script

children.description: Structured merge or script configuration for `strategy: Patch`. Required when `strategy` is `Patch`, rejected otherwise.
children.name: patch

children.description: Unix permission bits (e.g. "600", "644") to apply after deployment.
children.name: permissions

children.description: When true, the source file is local-only: auto-added to .gitignore, silently skipped on machines where it doesn't exist.
children.name: private

children.description: Path to the source file, relative to the module directory. Not required when `strategy` is `Patch`; required otherwise.
children.name: source

children.description: Per-file deployment strategy override. Omitted, the module-wide default applies.
children.name: strategy

children.description: Destination path on the machine. A leading `~` expands to the home directory.
children.name: target

children.description: Manager-specific package name aliases (e.g. `{apt: "neovim", brew: "neovim"}`) for a package named differently across managers.
children.name: aliases

children.description: Skip the install script if this path already exists. A leading `~` expands to the home directory; a relative path resolves against the script's working directory. Existence follows symlinks. Only meaningful for a `prefer: [script]` install; ignored otherwise.
children.name: creates

children.description: Package managers to never use for this package, even if otherwise available and preferred by the profile.
children.name: deny

children.description: Minimum acceptable installed version, loosely parsed (`"1.2"`, `"1"`). A version below this is treated as not satisfying the module.
children.name: minVersion

children.description: The package name as the chosen manager knows it.
children.name: name

children.description: Run the install script only if this command exits zero. A non-zero exit skips the install (the condition for installing was not met). Only meaningful for a `prefer: [script]` install; ignored for manager-backed installs (those are idempotent via the manager's installed-package query).
children.name: onlyIf

children.description: Platform tags gating this package alone. Empty means install on every platform the module itself is not already gated off of.
children.name: platforms

children.description: Manager preference order for this package, overriding the profile's default manager priority (e.g. `[brew, apt]`, or `[script]` to force the install script below).
children.name: prefer

children.description: Shell script to run instead of a manager install, selected via `prefer: [script]`.
children.name: script

children.description: Run the install script only if this command exits NON-zero. A zero exit (success) skips the install (the package already appears present). Only meaningful for a `prefer: [script]` install; ignored otherwise.
children.name: unless

fields.description: Platform tags gating the whole module. When non-empty and the current platform matches none of them, the module is skipped entirely (it appears as a skipped action rather than vanishing). Tags are matched against the machine's OS, distro, and arch; use `macos` for macOS.
fields.name: platforms

children.description: Run when a watched file changes on disk (requires `daemon.reconcile.onChange`).
children.name: onChange

variants.description: A bare command string, run with the platform's default shell and no timeout/guard.
variants.name: string

children.description: Treat a non-zero exit as success and continue reconciliation instead of failing the run. Default: `false`.
children.name: continueOnError

children.description: Skip the script if this path already exists. A leading `~` expands to the home directory; a relative path resolves against the script's working directory. Existence follows symlinks.
children.name: creates

children.description: Kill the script if it produces no stdout/stderr output for this duration. Prevents scripts from silently hanging on unresponsive resources. Format: "30s", "2m", etc. If unset, no idle timeout is enforced.
children.name: idleTimeout

children.description: Run the script attached to the terminal (inherited stdin/stdout/stderr, no spinner, no output capture, no idle timeout) so it can prompt the user — e.g. `echo "press Enter when done"; read`. Requires a TTY: when stdin is not a terminal (CI, piped input, or any daemon-run phase) the script is skipped with a warning rather than hanging on instant EOF.
children.name: interactive

children.description: Run the script only if this command exits zero. A non-zero exit skips the script (the condition for running was not met). Evaluated with the same shell, working directory, and environment as the body.
children.name: onlyIf

children.description: The command or script body to run.
children.name: run

children.description: Interpreter to use for inline commands. Ignored (and rejected) on file scripts.
children.name: shell

children.description: Kill the script if it runs longer than this duration (`"30s"`, `"2m"`). Unset means no timeout.
children.name: timeout

children.description: Run the script only if this command exits NON-zero. A zero exit (success) skips the script (the guarded state already holds). Evaluated with the same shell, working directory, and environment as the body.
children.name: unless

children.description: Working directory for the script. By default every lifecycle script runs in the user's home directory — never the config source tree — so a relative write can't pollute the user's GitOps repo. Set `workdir` to override: a leading `~` expands to home and `$VAR`/`${VAR}` expand against the script environment (which always carries `$CFGD_MODULE_DIR` and `$CFGD_CONFIG_DIR`), so `workdir: ~/.local/share/app`, `workdir: $CFGD_MODULE_DIR`, or an absolute path all work.
children.name: workdir
